messages:
Mike: Ran a 90m nsys run on ded-4 (A100) against the nightly inference job. Seeing a recurring p99 tail spike (~40-60ms) for 512-token requests. Timeline shows gaps in kernel launches right after a KV-cache sweep event.

Olga: Can you drop the trace link and a short command? :eyes:

Mike: Uploaded to artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/runs/1942506789. Command for capture was:```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas --output=/tmp/nsys_run \n  --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaKernelLaunch start,end \n  ./run_infer.sh --seq-len 512 --batch 1
```

Santiago: Quick thought — does the queue time balloon during those windows? If queue_time > compute_time the batcher could be folding requests oddly.

Kevin: Looked at the trace briefly: kernel selector flips from `matmul_fwd_small` -> `matmul_fwd_generic` mid-run. That change alone increases kernel time and may amplify the tail. Could be sensitive to padding or an unexpected dim.

Anna: I see a KV sweep at ~T+00:42 in the perfetto timeline. KV cache hitrate drops from ~98% to ~67% for ~6s, which correlates exactly with the latency spikes.

PerfBot: Regression detected — p99 latency +28% between commits a1b2c3d -> f4e5d6c. Top modified files: runtime/scheduler.cpp, kernels/matmul_opt.cu. Full diff: https://ci.internal/diffs/1942506789

Santiago: Can we reproduce deterministically? Try the workload generator with `--fixed-seed` and stable client timings so we can align traces.

Mike: Did a seeded run. Spike reproduces. Noticed a ~3-4ms host CPU stall before the problematic kernel launch in the nsys timeline (CPU wake/submit delay).

Olga: That smells like lock contention or priority inversion — maybe the KV sweep thread is pegging a core and delaying the launcher thread. What is sweep niceness?

Kevin: On the dev rig it was default. Quick experiment idea: lower sweep thread priority (nice +10) or pin it to a separate core and see if launch latency improves. Also worth trying forcing the kernel choice via env to see if selector hysteresis is the culprit: `KERNEL_SELECT=matmul_fwd_small` for a run.

Anna: If the KV hitrate drop is real, it explains extra cache misses and padding variance which can flip kernel heuristics. I'll extract the kv hitrate timeseries and batch size distribution for the same interval.

Santiago: I'll run three traces forcing the small matmul kernel and three without, same seed. If forced kernel eliminates the p99 spike, then we have two orthogonal issues: selector hysteresis + sweep-induced timing noise.

Mike: Good plan. If both factors contribute, short-term mitigation could be raising selector hysteresis thresholds or reverting the scheduler tweak in f4e5d6c that tightened launch ordering. Longer term we need improved backpressure so KV GC doesn't run mid-window.

Olga: Action items: 1) Santiago: forced-kernel traces (owner). 2) Kevin: try lowering sweep priority / CPU pinning on repro rig (owner). 3) Anna: kv hitrate + batch dist extraction (owner). 4) Mike: open perf issue with traces + nsys/perfetto links and tag runtime/scheduler + kernels.

Kevin: I'll post results by EOD. If lowering sweep priority helps, it's a quick rollback candidate. :thumbsup:

PerfBot: Attached artifact summary and flamegraph: https://artifacts.internal/perf/1942506789/flame.html

Mike: Thanks all. If someone finds a quick config fix, call it out here and we'll roll a canary to staging. Otherwise we'll follow the action items. :party-parrot:
